claim: the launch was moved before the review came in
note: The clip uses the claim's own words to deny it. Word overlap is near total.

judgements.quote: We did not move the launch before the review came in. That is not what happened.
Yes — the launch went out, and the review landed a week after it.

note: A denial that reads as an assertion if only the content words are matched.

judgements.quote: People keep saying she stopped taking the medication. She never stopped.

claim: they shipped without a security review
note: A counterfactual. Every content word is present and nothing is asserted.

judgements.quote: If we had shipped without a security review, this is exactly what it would look like.
Suppose they shipped without a security review — what would you expect to see?

note: A proposal, not a fact. The tense is the only signal.

judgements.quote: The proposal is that the council sells the building and leases it back.

claim: the company knew about the defect
note: Somebody else's claim, quoted. The speaker is reporting an accusation, not making one.

judgements.quote: Their lawyer stood up and said the company knew about the defect. That is her case, not mine.
We had the defect report on file in March and shipped in May.

note: Hearsay about hearsay, with the claim's words intact.

judgements.quote: The rumour going round was that he was asked to resign. Nobody has confirmed it.

note: Right shape, different person. A judge matching on the act will take it.

judgements.quote: The chief financial officer apologised at the end of the call.

claim: the Oxford branch closed in March
note: Right act, right month, different place.

judgements.quote: The Cambridge branch closed in March and the staff were moved.

note: True once and not now. A claim about the present, evidence about the past.

judgements.quote: The service was down for most of last winter. It has been fine since February.

note: Asserted and then narrowed until nothing of the claim survives.

judgements.quote: The budget was cut — well, the draft was, and then it was put straight back before anyone signed anything.
We took four hundred thousand out of the budget and it has not gone back.

claim: he admitted the delay and blamed the supplier
note: Two clauses. The clip carries one in the claim's own words and is silent on the other, so it is lexically near and semantically half.

judgements.quote: I admitted the delay the moment I knew. That one is on us and I am not dressing it up.
It was late, and it was late because the supplier missed two shipments.

claim: the report was commissioned and then buried
note: Supports the commissioning and says nothing about what followed.

judgements.quote: We commissioned the report in the spring.

claim: rent is the reason people leave the city
note: Maximum vocabulary overlap, no entailment — what defeats BM25 alone. The second clip is the harder case: the claim's words and its subject, with the causal link stated and then explicitly withheld.

judgements.quote: Rent, city, leaving, people — these are the words everyone uses and nobody explains.
Rent in this city went up again and a lot of the people I know have left. I am not saying one caused the other.

claim: the meeting was on the Tuesday
note: Said and corrected in one breath. A judge reading the first half takes it.

judgements.quote: The meeting was on the Tuesday — no, sorry, the Thursday. Tuesday was the site visit.

claim: she weighed what leaving would save against who it would cost
note: A control where the support is inferential: nothing in the clip uses the claim's words, and the two prices are both in the sentence. REVISED — the claim read "she priced the move in rent because the other price was harder to say", which the clip does not establish: it never says why she named rent first, and a reason for a choice is an interpretation of the speaker, not a thing said. The old note called it "stated plainly" and it was not stated at all. The judge refusing it is what prompted the re-read; the re-read is what changed it. See eval/README.md on when that is allowed.

judgements.quote: If I leave, rent halves and I lose everyone I would call at two in the morning.

claim: the launch moved because the review was going to fail
note: A control where the support is causal rather than restated.

judgements.quote: We moved it because we knew the review was going to come back red.

claim: nobody wanted to be the one to say it
note: A control that an over-cautious judge may wrongly reject.

judgements.quote: Everyone in that room knew, and not one of us put a hand up.

note: A control stated as a plain fact, with none of the hedging the near misses carry.

judgements.quote: They missed the March shipment and then they missed the April one.

claim: the house is the thing actually being chosen
note: A control where support is implied rather than stated, which an over-literal judge rejects.

judgements.quote: The house has a room that gets sun until four. I have thought about it more than I have thought about the job.
